entries.sanskrit:
चतुर्थे तु चतुर्धोक्ता लया नैमित्तिकादयः ।

तत्र संसार-निस्तारो हरि-कीर्त्यैव वर्ण्यते ॥

कलि-दोष-निवर्तकं हरि-नाम-सङ्कीर्तनादिकं स एव च कलौ परमो धर्म इति प्रश्न-द्वयस्योत्तरम् उक्तम् । यच् चान्यत् पृष्टं प्रलय-कल्पयोर् मानं ब्रूहीति [भा।पु। ३.१.११] तद् इदानीं तृतीय-स्कन्धोक्त-काल-मानानुवाद-पूर्वकं निरूपयति—काल इति । स कालः परमाणुर् वै यो भुङ्क्ते परमाणुतां [भा।पु। ३.११.४] इत्य्-आदिना कालः कथितः । 


> चत्वारि त्रीणि द्वे चैकं कृतादिषु यथा-क्रमम् ।   
> सङ्ख्यातानि सहस्राणि द्वि-गुणानि शतानि च ॥ [भा।पु। ३.११.१९] इति युग-मानं कथितम् ॥१॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
कालस् ते परमाण्व्-आदिर् द्वि-परार्धावधिर् नृप ।  
कथितो युग-मानं च शृणु कल्प-लयाव् अपि ॥
entries.literal_english: In the Fourth Canto the four kinds of dissolution—beginning with the occasional dissolution—are described. The means of deliverance from saṃsāra is also described: glorification of Hari alone removes the faults of Kali. This answers the two questions: saṅkīrtana of Hari’s name and the like is the supreme dharma in Kali.

kālas te paramāṇv-ādir dvi-parārdhāvadhir nṛpa |
kathito yuga-mānaṃ ca śṛṇu kalpa-layāv api ||

entries.sanskrit: तत्र कल्प-मानम् आह—चतुर्-युगेति । यत्र चतुर्दश मनवः क्रमेण भवन्ति ॥२॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
चतुर्-युग-सहस्रं तु ब्रह्मणो दिनम् उच्यते ।  
स कल्पो यत्र मनवश् चतुर्दश विशाम्-पते ॥
word_for_word: a thousand cycles of four ages
entries.literal_english: He states the measure of a kalpa: a thousand cycles of four ages make one day of Brahmā. In that kalpa fourteen Manus arise successively.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
catur-yuga-sahasraṃ tu brahmaṇo dinam ucyate |
sa kalpo yatra manavaś caturdaśa viśām-pate ||

entries.sanskrit: प्रलयस् तु चतुर्-विधः—नैमित्तिकः, प्राकृतिकः, आत्यन्तिकः, नित्यश् चेति । तत्र नैमित्तिकं प्रलयं मान-सहितम् आह—तद् अन्त इति द्वाभ्याम् । तावान् चतुर्-युग-सहस्र-प्रमाणः । सैव ब्राह्मी रात्रिः ॥३॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तद्-अन्ते प्रलयस् तावान् ब्राह्मी रात्रिर् उदाहृता ।  
त्रयो लोका इमे तत्र कल्पन्ते प्रलयाय हि ॥
entries.literal_english: Dissolution is fourfold: occasional, material, ultimate, and constant. He first gives the measure of the occasional dissolution: it lasts as long as a thousand cycles of four ages, the night of Brahmā. At that time these three worlds prepare for dissolution.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
tad-ante pralayas tāvān brāhmī rātrir udāhṛtā |
trayo lokā ime tatra kalpante pralayāya hi ||

entries.sanskrit: नैमित्तिकत्वं दर्शयति । यत्र यदा विश्व-सृक् श्री-नारायणो विश्वम् आत्म-सात्-कृत्य स्वस्मिन्न् उपसंहृत्य शेते, आत्म-भूर् ब्रह्मा च तस्मिन् शेते । तयोर् अभेद-विवक्षया वा ब्रह्मण एवानन्तासनत्वम् उक्तम् । ब्रह्मणो निद्रां निमित्ती-कृत्य प्रवर्तमानो लोक-त्रय-प्रलयो नैमित्तिक इत्य् आर्थः ॥४॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
एष नैमित्तिकः प्रोक्तः प्रलयो यत्र विश्व-सृक् ।  
शेतेऽनन्तासनो विश्वम् आत्मसात्-कृत्य चात्म-भूः ॥
word_for_word: having absorbed the universe into himself
entries.literal_english: This is called the occasional dissolution: when the creator of the universe, Śrī Nārāyaṇa, absorbs the universe into himself and lies upon Ananta’s couch, Brahmā, the self-born, also lies in him. Because their non-difference is intended, the statement may also be understood as Brahmā alone lying in Nārāyaṇa.

entries.transliteration:
eṣa naimittikaḥ proktaḥ pralayo yatra viśva-sṛk |
śete’nantāsano viśvam ātmasāt-kṛtya cātma-bhūḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: प्राकृतिकं प्रलयम् आह द्वाभ्याम्, द्वि-परार्धे तु ब्रह्मण आयुषि । सप्त-प्रकृतयो महद्-अहङ्कार-पञ्च-तन्-मात्राणि ॥५॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
द्वि-परार्धे त्व् अतिक्रान्ते ब्रह्मणः परमेष्ठिनः ।  
तदा प्रकृतयः सप्त कल्पन्ते प्रलयाय वै ॥
word_for_word: at the end of two parārdhas
mahat, ego and the five subtle elements
entries.literal_english: He describes the material dissolution: it occurs at the end of Brahmā’s lifespan of two parārdhas. The seven material principles are mahat, ahaṅkāra, and the five tan-mātras.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
dvi-parārdhe tv atikrānte brahmaṇaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ |
tadā prakṛtayaḥ sapta kalpante pralayāya vai ||

entries.sanskrit: सङ्घातो महद्-आदि-कार्य-भूतः, प्रकृतीनां तत्-कार्य-ब्रह्माण्डस्य च प्रलयात् प्राकृतिक इत्य् अर्थः । विघाते विघात-कारणे उपसादिते सति ॥६॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
एष प्राकृतिको राजन् प्रलयो यत्र लीयते ।  
अण्ड-कोषस् तु सङ्घातो विघात उपसादिते ॥
word_for_word: formed from the effects beginning with mahat
because of the dissolution of the material principles
has been brought near or effected
entries.literal_english: The aggregate formed from the effects beginning with mahat dissolves because the material principles and their product, the universe, dissolve. ‘When the cause of destruction is effected’ means when that dissolution has been brought about.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
eṣa prākṛtiko rājan pralayo yatra līyate |
aṇḍa-koṣas tu saṅghāto vighāta upasādite ||

entries.sanskrit: तद् एवाह—पर्जन्य इत्य्-आदिना बुद्धीन्द्रियार्थ-रूपेणेत्य् अतः प्राक्तनेन ग्रन्थेन ॥७॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
पर्जन्यः शत-वर्षाणि भूमौ राजन् न वर्षति ।  
तदा निरन्ने ह्य् अन्योन्यं भक्ष्यमाणाः क्षुधार्दिताः ॥
word_for_word: in the forms of intelligence, senses and objects
entries.literal_english: He states the same point beginning with ‘the rain cloud,’ connecting it with the preceding passage that described the forms of intelligence, the senses, and their objects.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
parjanyaḥ śata-varṣāṇi bhūmau rājan na varṣati |
tadā niranne hy anyonyaṃ bhakṣyamāṇāḥ kṣudhārditāḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: सामुद्रादिकं सर्वं रसं रविः ॥८॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
क्षयं यास्यन्ति शनकैः कालेनोपद्रुताः प्रजाः ।  
सामुद्रं दैहिकं भौमं रसं सांवर्तको रविः ॥
entries.literal_english: The sun draws up all liquid essence, including that of the ocean and other waters.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
kṣayaṃ yāsyanti śanakaiḥ kālenopadrutāḥ prajāḥ |
sāmudraṃ daihikaṃ bhaumaṃ rasaṃ sāṃvartako raviḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: पिबते आकर्षति ॥८॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
रश्मिभिः पिबते घोरैः सर्वं नैव विमुञ्चति ।  
ततः संवर्तको वह्निः सङ्कर्षण-मुखोत्थितः ॥
entries.literal_english: ‘Drinks’ means ‘draws toward itself.’
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
raśmibhiḥ pibate ghoraiḥ sarvaṃ naiva vimuñcati |
tataḥ saṃvartako vahniḥ saṅkarṣaṇa-mukhotthitaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: अनिल-वेगोत्थो वायु-वेगोद्भूतः । “अनिल-वेगो वा” इति पाठे अनिलेन वेगो यस्य सः, वाः रविणा रश्मिभिः पीतम् उदकं च दहतीत्य् अर्थः । “अनिल-वेगो वै” इति तु पाठः सु-गमः । भू-विवरान् पातालादीन् शून्यान् रविणा दैहिक-रसाकर्षणात् प्राणि-रहितान् । शिखाभिर् ज्वालाभिः ॥१०॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
दहत्य् अनिल-वेगोत्थः शून्यान् भू-विवरान् अथ ।  
उपर्य् अधः समन्ताच् च शिखाभिर् वह्नि-सूर्ययोः ॥
word_for_word: arisen from the speed of the wind
produced by the force of the air
entries.literal_english: The wind arises from the speed of the air. In the reading ‘whose speed is the wind,’ the water drunk by the sun’s rays is then burned. The clearer reading is ‘indeed produced by the wind’s force.’ The sun’s rays dry the hollows of the earth, such as the lower regions, making them empty of living beings, and burn them with flames.

entries.transliteration:
dahaty anila-vegotthaḥ śūnyān bhū-vivarān atha |
upary adhaḥ samantāc ca śikhābhir vahni-sūryayoḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: किञ्चिद् अधिकं वर्षाणां शतम् । सांवर्तकः प्रलय-हेतुः परो वायुर् वाति तदा रजसावृतं खं धूम्रं भवति ॥११॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
दह्यमानं विभात्य् अण्डं दग्ध-गोमय-पिण्ड-वत् ।  
ततः प्रचण्ड-पवनो वर्षाणाम् अधिकं शतम् ॥
entries.literal_english: The period is a little more than one hundred years. Then the superior Saṃvartaka wind, the cause of dissolution, blows. The sky becomes covered with dust raised by rajas and appears smoky.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
dahyamānaṃ vibhāty aṇḍaṃ dagdha-gomaya-piṇḍa-vat |
tataḥ pracaṇḍa-pavano varṣāṇām adhikaṃ śatam ||

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
परः सांवर्तको वाति धूम्रं खं रजसावृतम् ।  
ततो मेघ-कुलान्य् अङ्ग चित्र-वर्णान्य् अनेकशः ॥
entries.literal_english: No commentary.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. No separate Śrīdhara commentary is present in the pinned source.
entries.transliteration:
paraḥ sāṃvartako vāti dhūmraṃ khaṃ rajasāvṛtam |
tato megha-kulāny aṅga citra-varṇāny anekaśaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: रभस-स्वनैस् तीव्र-गर्जितैः । ब्रह्माण्ड-विवरम् अध्यगतं विश्वम् एकोदकम् अकार्णवोदक-व्याप्तं भवति ॥१३॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
शतं वर्षाणि वर्षन्ति नदन्ति रभस-स्वनैः ।  
तत एकोदकं विश्वं ब्रह्माण्ड-विवरान्तरम् ॥
word_for_word: the universe becomes one mass of water
filled with water extending to the ocean
entries.literal_english: With violent sounds and fierce thunder, the water fills the hollow of the cosmic egg. The entire universe becomes one mass of water, filled with water extending everywhere like an ocean.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
śataṃ varṣāṇi varṣanti nadanti rabhasa-svanaiḥ |
tata ekodakaṃ viśvaṃ brahmāṇḍa-vivarāntaram ||

entries.sanskrit: उद-प्लवे उदकेनाप्लवे सति । प्रलयत्वायाभावाय ॥१४॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तदा भूमेर् गन्ध-गुणं ग्रसन्त्य् आप उद-प्लवे ।  
ग्रस्त-गन्धा तु पृथिवी प्रलयत्वाय कल्पते ॥
word_for_word: when it is flooded with water
entries.literal_english: ‘When it is flooded’ means when it is covered by water. The inundation serves as the condition by which the universe becomes dissolved and its manifest form becomes absent.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
tadā bhūmer gandha-guṇaṃ grasanty āpa uda-plave |
grasta-gandhā tu pṛthivī pralayatvāya kalpate ||

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
अपां रसम् अथो तेजस् ता लीयन्तेऽथ नीरसाः ।  
ग्रसते तेजसो रूपं वायुस् तद्-रहितं तदा ॥
entries.literal_english: No commentary.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. No separate Śrīdhara commentary is present in the pinned source.
entries.transliteration:
apāṃ rasam atho tejas tā līyante’tha nīrasāḥ |
grasate tejaso rūpaṃ vāyus tad-rahitaṃ tadā ||

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
लीयते चानिले तेजो वायोः खं ग्रसते गुणम् ।  
स वै विशति खं राजंस् ततश् च नभसो गुणम् ॥
entries.literal_english: No commentary.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. No separate Śrīdhara commentary is present in the pinned source.
entries.transliteration:
līyate cānile tejo vāyoḥ khaṃ grasate guṇam |
sa vai viśati khaṃ rājaṃs tataś ca nabhaso guṇam ||

entries.sanskrit: भूतादिस् तामसो ऽहङ्कारः । गुणैर् वृत्तिभिः सह ॥१७॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
शब्दं ग्रसति भूतादिर् नभस् तम् अनु लीयते ।  
तैजसश् चेन्द्रियाण्य् अङ्ग देवान् वैकारिको गुणैः ॥
entries.literal_english: Bhūtādi is the tamasic ego, together with its qualities and functions.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
śabdaṃ grasati bhūtādir nabhas tam anu līyate |
taijasaś cendriyāṇy aṅga devān vaikāriko guṇaiḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: अव्याकृतं प्रधानम् ॥१८॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
महान् ग्रसत्य् अहङ्कारं गुणाः सत्त्वादयश् च तम् ।  
ग्रसतेऽव्याकृतं राजन् गुणान् कालेन चोदितम् ॥
entries.literal_english: The unmanifest is the pradhāna, primordial material nature.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
mahān grasaty ahaṅkāraṃ guṇāḥ sattvādayaś ca tam |
grasate’vyākṛtaṃ rājan guṇān kālena coditam ||

entries.sanskrit: तस्य तु लयो नास्तीत्य् आह—तस्येति । काल-वयवैर् अहो-रात्रादिभिः । गुणा भाव-विकाराः। परिणामो विपरिणामः । अव्यक्तम् अस्तित्व-विकार-शून्यम् । नित्यं सर्वदैक-रूपम्, ह्रास-वृद्धि-रहितम् इत्य् अर्थः । अव्ययम् अपक्षय-शून्यम् । सर्वत्र हेतुः—कारणम् इति ।
entries.main_sanskrit:
न तस्य कालावयवैः परिणामादयो गुणाः ।  
अनाद्य् अनन्तम् अव्यक्तं नित्यं कारणम् अव्ययम् ॥
entries.literal_english: He says that the unmanifest itself does not dissolve. The divisions of time, such as day and night, are modifications of changing existence; the qualities are also transformations. The unmanifest is free from modification of existence, always of one nature, without increase or decrease, and undecaying. It is the cause everywhere.

entries.transliteration:
na tasya kālāvayavaiḥ pariṇāmādayo guṇāḥ |
anādy anantam avyaktaṃ nityaṃ kāraṇam avyayam ||

entries.sanskrit: किं च, वाग्-आदि-गोचरस्य स-विशेषस्य विकारा भवन्ति, इदं तु न तथेत्य् आह—न यत्रेति द्वाभ्याम् । लोक-कल्पो लोक-रूपः सन्निवेशो रचना-विशेषो नास्ति ॥२०॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
न यत्र वाचो न मनो न सत्त्वं

तमो रजो वा महद्-आदयोऽमी ।

न प्राण-बुद्धीन्द्रिय-देवता वा

न सन्निवेशः खलु लोक-कल्पः ॥
word_for_word: of what is accessible to speech and the senses
having the form of a world
entries.literal_english: Things possessing distinctions and accessible to speech and the other senses undergo transformations; the unmanifest does not. There is no arrangement, configuration, or special construction in it that can be called a world.

entries.transliteration:
na yatra vāco na mano na sattvaṃ

tamo rajo vā mahad-ādayo’mī |

na prāṇa-buddhīndriya-devatā vā

na sanniveśaḥ khalu loka-kalpaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: स्वप्न-जाग्रत् स्वप्न-जागरावस्था-युक्तम् । संसुप्त-वद् इन्द्रियाभावात् । शून्य-सादृश्ये हेतुः—अप्रतर्क्यम् । न पुनः शून्यम् एवेत्य् आह—तद् इति ॥२१॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
न स्वप्न-जाग्रन् न च तत् सुषुप्तं

न खं जलं भूर् अनिलोऽग्निर् अर्कः ।

संसुप्त-वच् छून्य-वद् अप्रतर्क्यं

तन् मूल-भूतं पदम् आमनन्ति ॥
word_for_word: not earth and the other elements
entries.literal_english: It is neither the dream-waking state nor deep sleep; it is not space, water, earth, air, fire, or the sun. Because the senses are absent it resembles deep sleep, and because it is inconceivable it resembles emptiness, but it is not mere emptiness. It is in truth inconceivable in every respect, the fundamental basis of all, the place where the world dissolves and which yogīs know and liberated souls attain. The source’s footnote explains that this distinguishes it from the jīva, inert matter, and the ordinary states of consciousness.

na svapna-jāgran na ca tat suṣuptaṃ

na khaṃ jalaṃ bhūr anilo’gnir arkaḥ |

saṃsupta-vac chūnya-vad apratarkyaṃ

tan mūla-bhūtaṃ padam āmananti ||

entries.sanskrit: उपसंहरति—लय इति । शक्तयः सत्त्वादयः ॥२२॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
लयः प्राकृतिको ह्य् एष पुरुषाव्यक्तयोर् यदा ।  
शक्तयः सम्प्रलीयन्ते विवशाः काल-विद्रुताः ॥
entries.literal_english: He concludes: dissolution is the absorption of the powers beginning with sattva.

entries.transliteration:
layaḥ prākṛtiko hy eṣa puruṣāvyaktayor yadā |
śaktayaḥ sampralīyante vivaśāḥ kāla-vidrutāḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: आत्यन्तिकं लयम् आह—बुद्धीन्द्रियेति द्वदशभिः । आत्यन्तिक-लयो मोक्षः स च ब्रह्म-ज्ञानेन सर्व-प्रपञ्च-लयात्मकः । न च प्रपञ्चस्यात्मवत् सत्यत्वे लयः सम्भवतीति ज्ञान-रूपाद् ब्रह्मणः पृथग्-भूतस्य तस्यासत्त्वम् उपपादयति । बुद्धिश् चेन्द्रियाणि चार्थाश् चेत्य् एवं ग्राहक-करण-ग्राह्य-रूपेण तेषाम् आश्रय-भूतं ज्ञानम् एव भाति, न पृथक् । तत्र हेतुम् आह—दृश्यत्वाव्यतिरेकाभ्याम् इति । अतो यद् आद्य्-अन्तवत् तद् अवस्तु। अत्रैवं प्रयोगः—विमतं सन् न भवति । दृश्यत्वात् कारणाव्यतिरेकाद् आद्य्-अन्तवत्त्वाच् च, रज्जु-सर्पादिवद् इति ॥२३॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
बुद्धीन्द्रियार्थ-रूपेण ज्ञानं भाति तद्-आश्रयम् ।  
दृश्यत्वाव्यतिरेकाभ्याम् आद्य्-अन्तवद् अवस्तु यत् ॥
word_for_word: consisting in dissolution of the entire manifestation
because of being seen and non-different from the cause
entries.literal_english: He explains the ultimate dissolution in twelve verses. Ultimate dissolution is liberation, consisting in the dissolution of the entire manifestation through knowledge of Brahman. Intelligence, senses, and objects shine only as knowledge, the basis of the knower, instruments, and known—not as independent realities. Because they are seen and are non-different from their cause, whatever has a beginning and end is not ultimately real, like a rope-snake.

entries.transliteration:
buddhīndriyārtha-rūpeṇa jñānaṃ bhāti tad-āśrayam |
dṛśyatvāvyatirekābhyām ādy-antavad avastu yat ||

entries.sanskrit: तत्राव्यतिरेकं दृष्टान्तेन प्रपञ्चयति—दीप इति । दीप-चक्षू-रूपाणां तेजो-विशेषाणां तेजसो यथा न व्यतिरेकः, तथा धीः कर्त्री, खानि करणानि, मात्रा विषयाः, ऋताद् ब्रह्मणः पृथक् न स्युः, ब्रह्म-कार्यत्वात् । नन्व् एवं कार्य-कारणयोर् अभेदे कार्यासत्त्वे कारणस्याप्य् असत्त्वं प्रसज्जेत ? तत्राह—अन्यतमाद् इति कार्याद् अत्यन्त-व्यतिरिक्ताद् ब्रह्मणः । प्रपञ्चाद् ब्रह्मणोऽस्ति व्यतिरेकः, प्रपञ्चस्य तु ततो नास्ति व्यतिरेक इत्य् अर्थः ॥२४॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
दीपश् चक्षुश् च रूपं च ज्योतिषो न पृथग् भवेत् ।  
एवं धीः खानि मात्राश् च न स्युर् अन्यतमाद् ऋतात् ॥
word_for_word: of lamp, eye and visible form
entries.literal_english: He develops non-difference through an example: the light of a lamp, eye, and form is not separate from light itself. Similarly, intelligence as agent, the senses as instruments, and the tan-mātras as objects are not separate from Brahman because they are effects of Brahman. The world can be distinct from Brahman in the sense that it is not Brahman, but Brahman is never separate from the world; the effect cannot exist apart from its cause.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
dīpaś cakṣuś ca rūpaṃ ca jyotiṣo na pṛthag bhavet |
evaṃ dhīḥ khāni mātrāś ca na syur anyatamād ṛtāt ||

entries.sanskrit: यदा तु बुद्धेर् असत्त्वं, तदा तद्-अवस्थनां सुतराम् असत्त्वम् इत्य् आशयेनाह—बुद्धेर् इति । ननु विश्व-तैजस-प्राज्ञानाम् एता अवस्था न बुद्धेर् इत्य् आशण्ख्याह—माया-मात्रम् इति । इदं विश्व-तैजस-प्राज्ञ-रूपम् ॥२५॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
बुद्धेर् जागरणं स्वप्नः सुषुप्तिर् इति चोच्यते ।  
माया-मात्रम् इदं राजन् नानात्वं प्रत्यग्-आत्मनि ॥
word_for_word: the waking, dream and deep-sleep selves
entries.literal_english: When intelligence itself is unreal, its states are even more unreal. One may object that the waking, dream, and deep-sleep states do not belong to intelligence; he answers that these forms of Viśva, Taijasa, and Prājña are merely māyā.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
buddher jāgaraṇaṃ svapnaḥ suṣuptir iti cocyate |
māyā-mātram idaṃ rājan nānātvaṃ pratyag-ātmani ||

entries.sanskrit: आद्य्-अन्तवत्त्वाद् इत्य् अस्य हेतोर् असिद्धिम् आशङ्क्य सावयवत्वेन साधयति, यथेति । अवयवीति । यत् सावयवं तद् आद्य्-अन्त-वद् धटादि-वद् इत्य् अर्थः । अत उदयाप्ययाद् आद्य्-अन्त-वत्त्वाद् विश्वं सन्न भवतीत्य् अर्थः । यद् वा, पृथग् एवागमापायित्वाद् विश्वं मिथ्या । ब्रह्म तु तद् अवधित्वात् सत्यम् इत्य् अनेन साद्यते । दृष्टान्तस् तु पूर्वोक्त एव । यथा जल-धरा व्योम्नीति दृष्टान्तस् त्वागमापायि-तद्-अवधित्व-मात्रे, न तु मिथ्यात्वे ॥२६॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
यथा जल-धरा व्योम्नि भवन्ति न भवन्ति च ।  
ब्रह्मणीदं तथा विश्वम् अवयव्य् उदयाप्ययात् ॥
word_for_word: because of having beginning and end
the world is false or dependent
entries.literal_english: Since the proof ‘having beginning and end’ might be challenged, he establishes it by showing that the world is composite. Whatever has parts has a beginning and end, like a pot. Because the world arises and dissolves, it is not independently real. Alternatively, its separate appearance and disappearance show it to be dependent, whereas Brahman, the limit and ground of it, is real.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
yathā jala-dharā vyomni bhavanti na bhavanti ca |
brahmaṇīdaṃ tathā viśvam avayavy udayāpyayāt ||

entries.sanskrit: “अन्यतमाद् ऋतात्” इति प्रतिज्ञात-कारणस्य सत्यत्वम् उपपादयति—सत्यम् इति । अवयवः कारणं प्रोक्तः, वाचारंभणं विकारो नामधेयं मृत्तिकेत्य् एव सत्यं [छा।उ। ६.१.४] इत्य्-आदि-श्रुतिभिः । अत्र युक्तिम् अपि दर्शयति—विनेति । अङ्ग हे राजन् ! हि यस्माद् अर्थेनावयविना पृथग् एवावयवाः प्रतीयेरन् । यथा पटस्यावयवास् तन्तवः पटात् पृथक् प्रतीयन्ते तद्वद् इति ॥२७॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
सत्यं ह्य् अवयवः प्रोक्तः सर्वावयविनाम् इह ।

:
     एते इति तत्त्ववादि-पाठः।


विनार्थेन प्रतीयेरन् पटस्येवाङ्ग तन्तवः ॥
word_for_word: the modification is only a verbal designation
entries.literal_english: He establishes the truth of the cause promised by ‘from one of the real principles.’ Scripture says that the cause is real and the modification is merely a name arising in speech—‘the clay alone is real.’ He also gives reasoning: the parts of a whole are perceived separately from the whole, as threads are perceived separately from cloth. The source’s extended note explains that part and whole have a qualified difference within non-difference and that dependent cause-effect chains are not independent; only Bhagavān is fully independent.

entries.transliteration:
satyaṃ hy avayavaḥ proktaḥ sarvāvayavinām iha |

:
     ete iti tattvavādi-pāṭhaḥ|

vinārthena pratīyeran paṭasyevāṅga tantavaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit:
ननु कार्याभावे कारणत्वं ब्रह्मणः कुतो घटेत ? सत्यम्, तद् अपि नातीव सत्यम् इत्य् आह—यद् इति । सामान्यं कारणम्, विशेषः कार्यम्, तद्-रूपेणान्योऽन्यापाश्रयात् परस्परापेक्षत्वेन निरूपणासहत्वाद् इत्य् अर्थः । अतः कारणत्वम् अवधित्वं व्यापकत्वम् इत्य्-आदिकम् अपि यत् परापेक्षत्वाद् आद्य्-अन्तवत्, तत् सर्वम् अवस्त्व् इत्य् अर्थः । 

यद् वा, तत्रैव हेत्व्-अन्तरम् एतत् । यद् उपलभ्येत स भ्रमः, सामान्य-विशेष-रूपत्वात् स्वप्नवत् । अन्योन्यापाश्रयात् इतीदम् अपि हेत्व्-अन्तरं गुण-गुणि-विशेषण-विशेष्य-व्याप्य-व्यापकत्वादि-रूपेण परस्पराधीन-सिद्धित्वात् । तथा-भूत-स्वप्नवद् इति निगमनम् । अतो यद् आद्य्-अन्तवत् तत् सर्वम् अवस्त्व् इति ॥२८॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
यत् सामान्य-विशेषाभ्याम् उपलभ्येत स भ्रमः ।  
अन्योऽन्यापाश्रयात् सर्वम् आद्य्-अन्तवद् अवस्तु यत् ॥
word_for_word: in the absence of the effect
entries.literal_english: One might ask how Brahman can be called the cause when the effect is not ultimately real. He answers that the general cause and particular effect are defined through mutual dependence, so neither is independently established in that relation. Causality, pervasion, and similar relations are also dependent and therefore have beginning and end. What is perceived as general and particular is like a dream; it is not independently real.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
yat sāmānya-viśeṣābhyām upalabhyeta sa bhramaḥ |
anyo’nyāpāśrayāt sarvam ādy-antavad avastu yat ||

entries.sanskrit: तद् एवम् अनेकैर् हेतुभिः प्रपञ्चस्यासत्त्वं साधितम् । तत्र शङ्का, ननु प्रपञ्चस्यापि प्रकाशमानत्वाद् आत्म-वत् सत्त्वं किं न स्यात् ? इति तत्राह—विकार इति ख्यायमानः प्रकाशमानोऽपि विकारः प्रपञ्चः प्रत्यग्-आत्म-प्रकाशं विनाऽणु-मात्रोऽपि न निरूप्योऽस्ति । तं विना निरूप्यः स्याच् चेत् तर्हि सोऽपि चित्-समः स्यत्, चिद्-रूपेणात्मना समः स्व-प्रकाशो भवेत् । तथा च सति सोऽप्य् आत्मवत् स्यात् । एक-रूपः स्याद् इत्य् अर्थः ॥२९॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
विकारः ख्यायमानोऽपि प्रत्यग्-आत्मानम् अन्तरा ।  
न निरूप्योऽस्त्य् अणुर् अपि स्याच् चेच् चित्-सम आत्म-वत् ॥
word_for_word: without the light of the inner self
entries.literal_english: The unreality of the manifestation has been established by several reasons. Someone may object that the world is real because it appears, like the self. He answers: although the modification called the world appears, without the light of the inner self it cannot be identified even in the slightest degree. If it could be identified independently, it too would be consciousness and self-luminous like the self; it would then be one undivided reality like the self.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
vikāraḥ khyāyamāno’pi pratyag-ātmānam antarā |
na nirūpyo’sty aṇur api syāc cec cit-sama ātma-vat ||

entries.sanskrit: कुतः ? इत्य् अत आह—नहीति । ननु सत्यस्याप्य् आत्मनो जीव-ब्रह्म-रूपं नानात्वम् अस्त्य् एव तत्राह—यद्य् एवं नानात्वं मन्यते, तर्ह्य् अविद्वान् । कथं तर्हि तयोर् भेद-व्यवहार उपाधि-कृतः ? इत्य् आह—नानात्वम् इति । तत्र छिद्रयोर् घटाकाश-महाकाशयोर् इवेति परिच्छेदापरिच्छेदे दृष्टान्तः । ज्योतिषोर् आकाश-जलस्ययोः सूर्ययोर् इवेत्य् उपाधि-कृत-विकार-सद्-असद्-भावे । वातयोर् बाह्य-शरीर-स्थ-वाय्वोर् इवेति क्रिया-भेदे ॥३०॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
न हि सत्यस्य नानात्वम् अविद्वान् यदि मन्यते ।  
नानात्वं छिद्रयोर् यद्वज् ज्योतिषोर् वातयोर् इव ॥
entries.literal_english: He asks why diversity is not ultimately real. If one thinks that the true self is really diverse as individual soul and Brahman, one is uninformed. Their apparent difference is produced by limiting adjuncts: limitation and non-limitation are like pot-space and great space; the apparent difference between lights or between inner and outer air is likewise due to adjuncts and difference of activity.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
na hi satyasya nānātvam avidvān yadi manyate |
nānātvaṃ chidrayor yadvaj jyotiṣor vātayor iva ||

entries.sanskrit: ब्रह्मण एव प्रपञ्च-व्यवहारालम्बनत्वं दृष्टान्तेन स्पष्टयति—यथेति । क्रियाभिस् तत्-तद्-रचना-भेदैर् बहुधा कटक-कूण्डलादि-रूपेण । लौकिक-वैदिकैर् वचोभिः । जनैर् अहङ्कारोपहितैह् ॥३१॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
यथा हिरण्यं बहुधा समीयते

नृभिः क्रियाभिर् व्यवहार-वर्त्मसु ।

एवं वचोभिर् भगवान् अधोक्षजो

व्याख्यायते लौकिक-वैदिकैर् जनैः ॥
word_for_word: being the basis of worldly dealings
in forms such as bracelets and earrings
entries.literal_english: He clarifies by an example that Brahman alone is the basis of dealings with the manifestation. Through different activities, the one material becomes many forms such as bracelets and earrings; through worldly and Vedic words people designate them differently. Those dealings are made by people conditioned by ego.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
yathā hiraṇyaṃ bahudhā samīyate

nṛbhiḥ kriyābhir vyavahāra-vartmasu |

evaṃ vacobhir bhagavān adhokṣajo

vyākhyāyate laukika-vaidikair janaiḥ ||

entries.sanskrit:
नन्व् अहङ्कारस्य कथं ब्रह्म-स्वरूपावरणेन भेद-व्यवहार-हेतुत्वम्, तस्य स्व-कारण-भूत-ब्रह्मावरकत्वासंभवाद् आवरणे वा, स्वस्यापि प्रकाशासंभवात् ? इत्य् आशङ्क्य स-दृष्टान्तम् आह—यथा इति । अर्क-रश्मय एव मेघ-रूपेण परिणता वर्षन्ति । 


> अग्नौ प्रास्ताहुतिः सम्यग् आदित्यम् उपतिष्ठते ।   
> आदित्याज् जायते वृष्टिर् वृष्टेर् अन्नं ततः प्रजाः ॥ [मनु ३.७६]

इत्य्-आदि-वचनात् । तस्माद् अर्क-प्रभवः, अर्केणैव दर्शितः प्रकाशितश् च, तमः स्वरूप-भूतार्क-दर्शन-प्रतिबन्धको भवति । अहम् अहङ्कारो ब्रह्म-गुणो ब्रह्म-कार्य-भूत इत्य् अर्थः, तद्-ईक्षितस् तेनैव प्रकाशितश् च, आत्मनो जीवस्य आत्म-बन्धनो ब्रह्म-स्वरूप-दर्शन-प्रतिबन्धको भवति॥३२॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
यथा घनोऽर्क-प्रभवोऽर्क-दर्शितो

ह्य् अर्कांश-भूतस्य च चक्षुषस् तमः ।

एवं त्व् अहं ब्रह्म-गुणस् तद्-ईक्षितो

ब्रह्मांशकस्यात्मन आत्म-बन्धनः ॥
word_for_word: transformed into the form of clouds
entries.literal_english: He answers the doubt about how ego can cover Brahman and cause dealings in difference. The sun’s rays themselves become clouds and rain; arising from the sun and illumined by it, the cloud nevertheless blocks the sight of the sun. Likewise, ego is a quality and product of Brahman, illumined by Brahman, yet it binds the individual self and obstructs vision of Brahman’s nature.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
yathā ghano’rka-prabhavo’rka-darśito

hy arkāṃśa-bhūtasya ca cakṣuṣas tamaḥ |

evaṃ tv ahaṃ brahma-guṇas tad-īkṣito

brahmāṃśakasyātmana ātma-bandhanaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: अत एवाहङ्कार-नाशे स्वरूप-दर्शनं भवतीति, तेनैव दृष्टान्तेनाह—घन इति आत्मन उपाधिः । जिज्ञासया विचारेण । तर्हि तदा अनुस्मरेत्, ब्रह्माहम् इति पश्यतीत्य् अर्थः ॥३३॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
घनो यदार्क-प्रभवो विदीर्यते

चक्षुः स्वरूपं रविम् ईक्षते तदा ।

यदा ह्य् अहङ्कार उपाधिर् आत्मनो

जिज्ञासया नश्यति तर्ह्य् अनुस्मरेत् ॥
word_for_word: the limiting adjunct of the self
entries.literal_english: Therefore, when ego is destroyed, realization of one’s true nature occurs. The cloud is the example, and ego is the self’s limiting adjunct. Through inquiry, one should then remember and see, ‘I am Brahman.’
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
ghano yadārka-prabhavo vidīryate

cakṣuḥ svarūpaṃ ravim īkṣate tadā |

yadā hy ahaṅkāra upādhir ātmano

jijñāsayā naśyati tarhy anusmaret ||

entries.sanskrit: सोऽयम् आत्यन्तिकः प्रलय इत्य् उपसंहरति—यदैवम् इति । विवेक-हेतिना ज्ञान-शस्त्रेण । अहङ्करणम् एवात्म-बन्धनम् । अच्युतं परिपूर्णम् आत्मानम् अनुभवतीति तथा॥३४॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
यदैवम् एतेन विवेक-हेतिना

माया-मयाहङ्करणात्म-बन्धनम् ।

छित्त्वाच्युतात्मानुभवोऽवतिष्ठते

तम् आहुर् आत्यन्तिकम् अङ्ग सम्प्लवम् ॥
entries.literal_english: He concludes that this is the ultimate dissolution. With the sword of knowledge that produces discrimination, cutting the bondage of the self made by māyā in the form of ego, one remains established in realization of the complete, imperishable Self. This is called ultimate dissolution.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
yadaivam etena viveka-hetinā

māyā-mayāhaṅkaraṇātma-bandhanam |

chittvācyutātmānubhavo’vatiṣṭhate

tam āhur ātyantikam aṅga samplavam ||

entries.sanskrit: नित्य-प्रलयम् आह—नित्यदेति ॥३५॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
नित्यदा सर्व-भूतानां ब्रह्मादीनां परन्-तप ।  
उत्पत्ति-प्रलयाव् एके सूक्ष्म-ज्ञाः सम्प्रचक्षते ॥
entries.literal_english: He now states the constant dissolution, the change that occurs continually.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
nityadā sarva-bhūtānāṃ brahmādīnāṃ paran-tapa |
utpatti-pralayāv eke sūkṣma-jñāḥ sampracakṣate ||

entries.sanskrit: कुतः ? इत्य् अत आह—कालेति । परिणामिना नदी-प्रवाह-प्रदीप-ज्वालादीनां या उच्च-नीचावस्थास् ताः काल-रूप-स्रोतसो वेगेनाशु ह्रियमाणस्य देहादेर् दृश्यमानास् ता एव नित्यदा जन्म-प्रलय-हेतवो भवन्ति । देहः प्रतिक्षणं प्रध्वंसी, प्रतिक्षणम् अवस्थाभेदास्पदत्वात्, प्रदीपादि-वद् इत्य् अनुमानम् ॥३६॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
काल-स्रोतो-जवेनाशु ह्रियमाणस्य नित्यदा ।  
परिणामिनाम् अवस्थास् ता जन्म-प्रलय-हेतवः ॥
word_for_word: by the stream in the form of Time
entries.literal_english: He explains that the higher and lower states of changing things—such as the flow of a river or the flame of a lamp—are swiftly carried away by the stream of Time. These visible states of the body and other things become the causes of birth and dissolution at every moment. The body is destroyed moment by moment because it is the basis of changing states, as inferred from a lamp and similar examples.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
kāla-sroto-javenāśu hriyamāṇasya nityadā |
pariṇāminām avasthās tā janma-pralaya-hetavaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: ननु यदि प्रतिक्षणम् अवस्था भवन्ति तर्हि किं न दृष्यन्ते, अतो हेतुर् असिद्ध इत्य् आशङ्क्याह, अनाद्य्-अन्तवता कालेन जायमाना अवस्था नैव लक्ष्यन्ते, आकाशे गच्छतां ज्योतिषां चन्द्रादीनां गमनावस्थाविशेषा यथा नैव लक्ष्यन्ते तद्वत् । अतो यथा तेषां प्रदेशान्तर-प्राप्त्या प्रतिक्षणं गत्य्-अवस्थाः कल्प्यन्ते तद्वद् अत्रापि बाल्य-तारुण्यादि-दर्शनेन मध्य-वर्तिन्योऽवस्थाः कल्प्यन्त इति न हेतुर् असिद्ध इत्य् अर्थः ॥३७॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
अनाद्य्-अन्तवतानेन कालेनेश्वर-मूर्तिना ।  
अवस्था नैव दृश्यन्ते वियति ज्योतिषाम् इव ॥
entries.literal_english: One may object that if states arise every moment, they should be visible. He answers that states produced by beginningless and endless Time are not perceived individually, just as the successive movement of the moon and other luminaries through the sky is not perceived moment by moment. Their motion is inferred from their arrival in another region; similarly, intervening stages such as childhood and youth are inferred from what is observed.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
anādy-antavatānena kāleneśvara-mūrtinā |
avasthā naiva dṛśyante viyati jyotiṣām iva ||

entries.sanskrit: उपसंहरति—नित्य इति ॥३८॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
नित्यो नैमित्तिकश् चैव तथा प्राकृतिको लयः ।  
आत्यन्तिकश् च कथितः कालस्य गतिर् ईदृशी ॥
entries.literal_english: He concludes: this continual change is the constant dissolution.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
nityo naimittikaś caiva tathā prākṛtiko layaḥ |
ātyantikaś ca kathitaḥ kālasya gatir īdṛśī ||

entries.sanskrit: पुराणार्थम् उपसंहरति—एता इति । लीला-विषयाः कथा अजो ब्रह्मापि कार्त्स्न्येनाभिधातुं नेशः ॥३९॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
एताः कुरु-श्रेष्ठ जगद्-विधातुर्

नारायणस्याखिल-सत्त्व-धाम्नः ।

लीला-कथास् ते कथिताः समासतः

कार्त्स्न्येन नाजोऽप्य् अभिधातुम् ईशः ॥
entries.literal_english: He concludes the purport of the Purāṇa: the narratives of the Lord’s pastimes are so extensive that even the unborn Brahmā is unable to describe them in full.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
etāḥ kuru-śreṣṭha jagad-vidhātur

nārāyaṇasyākhila-sattva-dhāmnaḥ |

līlā-kathās te kathitāḥ samāsataḥ

kārtsnyena nājo’py abhidhātum īśaḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: ननु यदि साकल्येनाभिधातुं न शक्यन्ते, तर्हि किं तद्-अभिधानेन ? तत्राह—संसारेति । विविधं दुःखम् एव दवो दावानलः, तेनार्दितस्य पीडितस्य, अत उत्तितीर्षोः पुंसो भगवतो या लीलाह्, तासां कथाः, तासां रसह्, तन्-निषेवणम् अन्तरेणान्यः प्लवस् तरण-साधनं न भवेत्, उपायान्तरासंभवात् । तत्-कथा-श्रवणम् एव यथा-शक्ति निषेव्यम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥४०॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
संसार-सिन्धुम् अतिदुस्तरम् उत्तितीर्षोर्

नान्यः प्लवो भगवतः पुरुषोत्तमस्य ।

लीला-कथा-रस-निषेवनम् अन्तरेण

पुंसो भवेद् विविध-दुःख-दवार्दितस्य ॥
word_for_word: drinking the taste of the pastime narratives
tormented by the forest fire of varied suffering
entries.literal_english: If the pastimes cannot be described completely, why describe them? For a person tormented by the forest fire of varied suffering in saṃsāra and wishing to cross that extremely difficult ocean, there is no other boat than continuously relishing the narratives of Bhagavān’s pastimes. They should be heard and relished according to one’s capacity; no other means is available.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
saṃsāra-sindhum atidustaram uttitīrṣor

nānyaḥ plavo bhagavataḥ puruṣottamasya |

līlā-kathā-rasa-niṣevanam antareṇa

puṃso bhaved vividha-duḥkha-davārditasya ||

entries.sanskrit: श्रोतुर् आदर-दार्ध्याय संप्रदाय-प्रवृत्तिम् आह, पुराण-संहिताम् इति त्रिभिः ।
entries.main_sanskrit:
पुराण-संहिताम् एताम् ऋषिर् नारायणोऽव्ययः ।  
नारदाय पुरा प्राह कृष्ण-द्वैपायनाय सः ॥
entries.literal_english: To strengthen the hearer’s respect, he describes the transmission of the tradition in three verses. This Purāṇa compendium was formerly spoken by the imperishable sage Nārāyaṇa to Nārada, and Nārāyaṇa then spoke it to Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
purāṇa-saṃhitām etām ṛṣir nārāyaṇo’vyayaḥ |
nāradāya purā prāha kṛṣṇa-dvaipāyanāya saḥ ||

entries.sanskrit: स वै बादरायणः प्रीतः सन् मह्यम् इमां संहितां प्राहेति पूर्वेणान्वयः ।
entries.main_sanskrit:
स वै मह्यं महा-राज भगवान् बादरायणः ।  
इमां भागवतीं प्रीतः संहितां वेद-सम्मिताम् ॥
entries.literal_english: The connection is: that Bādarāyaṇa, being pleased, spoke this compendium to me.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved. Śrīdhara commentary translated from the pinned Devanāgarī source.
entries.transliteration:
sa vai mahyaṃ mahā-rāja bhagavān bādarāyaṇaḥ |
imāṃ bhāgavatīṃ prītaḥ saṃhitāṃ veda-sammitām ||

entries.sanskrit: असौ सूत इति पुरतः स्थितम् अङ्गुल्या निर्दिश्याह । नैमिषालये नैमिषारण्य-स्थाने ॥४३॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
इमां वक्ष्यत्य् असौ सूत ऋषिभ्यो नैमिषालये ।  
दीर्घ-सत्रे कुरु-श्रेष्ठ सम्पृष्टः शौनकादिभिः ॥
word_for_word: by Śaunaka and the other sages
entries.literal_english: ‘This Sūta’ means that he points with his finger to Sūta standing before him. He will speak this compendium to the sages in Naimiṣāraṇya, during the long sacrifice, when questioned by Śaunaka and the other sages.
